issue_context.body:
### `brew doctor` output

```shell
Error: /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Cellar/llama.cpp/4889 is not a directory
```

### Verification

- [x] My "`brew doctor` output" above says `Your system is ready to brew.` and am still able to reproduce my issue.
- [x] I ran `brew update` twice and am still able to reproduce my issue.
- [x] This issue's title and/or description do not reference a single formula e.g. `brew install wget`. If they do, open an issue at https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/issues/new/choose instead.

### `brew config` output

I am not sure how Ruby works. Does that `rescue` break the cycle? Because that means it returns only the first failing dependency, while the error message is saying about the list.

> why it doesn't give me the list of all broken packages in one go?

Because the patch you proposed catches the issue at the wrong level. @botantony's patch catches each individual error, while yours stops the `select` loop at the first error.

@abitrolly try this patch
```patch
diff --git a/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/linux/diagnostic.rb b/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/linux/diagnostic.rb
index 2aad96cc0c..7c580b2076 100644
--- a/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/linux/diagnostic.rb
+++ b/Library/Homebrew/extend/os/linux/diagnostic.rb
@@ -143,13 +143,24 @@ module OS
           return if gcc_dependents.empty?
 
           badly_linked = gcc_dependents.select do |dependent|
-            keg = Keg.new(dependent.prefix)
-            keg.binary_executable_or_library_files.any? do |binary|
-              paths = binary.rpaths
-              versioned_linkage = paths.any? { |path| path.match?(%r{lib/gcc/\d+$}) }
-              unversioned_linkage = paths.any? { |path| path.match?(%r{lib/gcc/current$}) }
-
-              versioned_linkage && !unversioned_linkage
+            # Keg.new() may raise an error if it is not a directory.
+            # As the result `brew doctor` may display `Error: <keg> is not a directory`
+            # instead of proper `doctor` information.
+            # There are other checks that test that, we can skip broken kegs.
+            list_element = dependent # HACK: `brew style` comlains about `begin` otherwise
+            begin
+              keg = Keg.new(dependent.prefix)
+              keg.binary_executable_or_library_files.any? do |binary|
+                paths = binary.rpaths
+                versioned_linkage = paths.any? { |path| path.match?(%r{lib/gcc/\d+$}) }
+                unversioned_linkage = paths.any? { |path| path.match?(%r{lib/gcc/current$}) }
+
+                versioned_linkage && !unversioned_linkage
+              end
+              # It would be nice to add error type to differentiate between
+              # `#{path} is not a valid keg` and `#{path} is not a directory` errors
+            rescue
+              list_element
             end
           end
           return if badly_linked.empty?
```

>  @botantony's patch catches each individual error, while yours stops the select loop at the first error.

I think the original code will work fine if you just replace
```ruby
dependent.prefix
```
here with
```ruby
dependent.any_installed_prefix
```
If you want to be sure, you can also try
```ruby
next unless dependent.any_installed_prefix.directory?
```
